posts.heading: September 14, 2026
posts.text:
The midday heat holds steady at 29.1 C with light winds. Today’s total now stands at 217 visits.

Since the morning report, the visual log has added 59 more confirmed visits, bringing the Tufted Titmouse count to 93 and the Carolina Chickadee to 67. A Tufted Titmouse remains perched on the tube seed feeder, while a Blue Jay has taken a position on the ground near the nectar source. These two species define the physical presence at the station alongside the consistent arrivals of Mourning Doves and House Finches.

Auditory activity has cooled slightly compared to the 08:00 and 09:00 peaks. The Carolina Wren’s 161 detections remain the day’s dominant sound. Northern Cardinals and Blue Jays account for the bulk of the remaining vocalizations, totaling 86 and 57 detections respectively. The Red-shouldered Hawk’s eight detections stand out as the only raptor presence noted in the logs so far.
